preamble: Palatalization of the voiceless dental/alveolar stop /t/ to the voiceless postalveolar affricate [tʃ] is a common phonetic process. This typically occurs before high front vowels like /i/, where the tongue body raises towards the palate.

examples.note: In the Mamean branch chain shift, Proto-Mayan *[t] shifted to [tʃ], displacing the original *[tʃ] which moved further to the retroflex [ʈʂ]. This change affected Mam, Tectitec, Awakatec, and Ixil. The shift is part of a cascade: *r > t, *t > tʃ, *tʃ > ʈʂ, *ʃ > ʂ.
Hoocąk c = /tʃ/; final vowel lost after affrication
Palatalization before *i; Chayuco and San Juan Colorado have the intermediate catyi
